name: PublishObject
description: Represents a complete or partial loaded presentation that is available for publishing to HTML. The PublishObject object is a member of the PublishObjects collection.
remarks: You can specify the content and attributes of the published presentation by setting various properties of the PublishObject object. For example, the SourceTypeproperty defines the portion of a loaded presentation to be published. The RangeStartproperty and the RangeEndproperty specify the range of slides to publish, and the SpeakerNotesproperty designates whether or not to publish the speaker's notes.

properties.name: Application
properties.description: Returns an Application object that represents the creator of the specified object.

properties.name: Parent
properties.description: Returns the parent object for the specified object.

properties.name: HTMLVersion
properties.description: Returns or sets the version of HTML for a published presentation. Read/write.

properties.name: SourceType
properties.description: Returns or sets the source type of the presentation to be published to HTML. Read/write.

properties.name: RangeStart
properties.description: Returns or sets the number of the first slide in a range of slides you are publishing as a Web presentation. Read/write.

properties.name: RangeEnd
properties.description: Returns or sets the number of the last slide in a range of slides you are publishing as a Web presentation. Read/write.

properties.name: SlideShowName
properties.description: Returns or sets the name of the custom slide show to be published as a Web presentation. Read/write.

properties.name: SpeakerNotes
properties.description: Determines whether speaker notes are to be published with the presentation. Read/write.

properties.name: FileName
properties.description: Returns or sets the path and file name of the Web presentation created when all or part of the active presentation is published. Read/write.

methods.name: Publish
methods.description: Creates a Web presentation (HTML format) from any loaded presentation. You can view the published presentation in a web browser.
